mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% while payrolls (PAYEMS) grow at less than 100,000 persons signals labor market tightness without robust hiring, which compresses wage growth and profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect reverses when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points within a single month signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not observed during non-panic periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% while consumer spending (GDPC1) grows less than 0.2% indicates a shift from consumption to savings, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 5% AND GDPC1 monthly change < 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is absent when unemployment is rising sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not observed during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 1% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 1% AND HOUST < previous month - 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is absent when commodity prices are rising sharply.
